title: [Performance][Model] Fuse MiniMax-M3 QK norm, RoPE and KV cache insertion
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

MiniMax-M3's attention preparation launches separate normalization, RoPE, and two cache-insertion operators. This change performs four Gemma RMSNorms, partial NeoX RoPE, and main K/V plus index K cache writes in one Triton kernel. Only Q and index Q are materialized. RoPE rows are read directly inside the kernel, eliminating the external gather as well.

Support both packed projections and separate QKV/index projections used by W8A8 models, without adding a concat/copy. Vectorize Q/K and index Q/K over contiguous head rows within one program per token.

Based on main `05fa3be5f`; independent of #15772. References: #15772 and vLLM's [`fusedMiniMaxQNormRopeKVInsertKernel`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7566d83bd35cdfd7cd3f9e521a005d2fc1ed1c33/csrc/libtorch_stable/fused_minimax_m3_qknorm_rope_kv_insert_kernel.cu).

Preserve independent main/index slot mappings, negative slots, graph padding, cache strides, and BF16 normalization rounding. Cache capacity (`num_blocks`) is dynamic and is not a kernel compilation parameter. Cache writes, indexer and sparse attention remain inside an opaque attention boundary, with no duplicate insertion calls.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Automatically enable for BF16 NPU input, matching 128-wide main/index heads, NeoX RoPE, matching norm epsilon and at most 512 tokens including padding. Both packed and separate index projections are supported. Other configurations retain the existing path. No new flags or environment variables.

### How was this patch tested?

A3 operator tests on host 197: CANN 9.2.0, torch 2.10.0, torch_npu 2.10.0.post4, triton 3.5.0 / triton_ascend 3.2.2. BF16, Q/KV/index heads 8/1/1, head dimension 128, rotary dimension 64, block size 128, 5392 blocks, separate index projection.

The baseline matches the model's separate-index operator chain (including runtime Q/K `1 + weight`, two index contiguous operations, two index Gemma RMSNorms, RoPE, and both cache-insertion calls). Timings cover the complete prepare/cache region; no gather or copy is moved outside measurement. Projection GEMMs and allocation are outside both paths.

| Tokens | Baseline (us) | Fused (us) | Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 32.73 | 3.07 | 10.67x |
| 4 | 37.40 | 3.45 | 10.85x |
| 8 | 41.71 | 3.66 | 11.41x |
| 16 | 50.96 | 4.55 | 11.20x |
| 32 | 59.96 | 6.66 | 9.01x |
| 64 | 64.47 | 8.48 | 7.60x |
| 128 | 67.47 | 11.34 | 5.95x |
| 192 | 76.05 | 14.40 | 5.28x |
| 256 | 86.53 | 17.50 | 4.95x |

```bash
pytest -q tests/ut/models/minimax_m3 \
  tests/e2e/pull_request/one_card/test_minimax_qknorm_rope_cache.py
# 188 passed, 2 skipped (FP8 requires A5)
pytest -sv tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/test_minimax_qknorm_rope_cache_performance.py \
  -o junit_family=legacy --junitxml=/tmp/minimax-qk-performance.xml
# 20 passed
```

The real compilation tests use an isolated real Triton JIT function and count both dispatch-cache variants and calls into the real compilation entry point:

- In one process, fixed BF16/layout: warm once, independently sweep launch tokens (1/4/8/16/32/64/128/192/256/512), actual tokens (`NUM_SLOTS`, including 0/1 and aligned/unaligned values), and cache blocks (3/64/5392/8192). All **25 cases retain exactly one variant and one compilation entry**. Cache writes also check that the runtime bound actually changes.
- Nine distinct layouts each compile once (dense, main/index row padding, strided positions, RoPE row padding, independent K/V/index block padding, packed projections). Revisiting all nine with different request sizes adds **zero variants or compilation entries**.
- Negative controls: restoring `tl.constexpr`, or removing `do_not_specialize` alone, each makes the reuse test fail on a second compiled variant. These controls ran in separate processes without changing the production file.

Correctness coverage includes guards/fallback, fake/dummy handling, separate projections without concat, insertion ordering, CPU-reference numerical comparisons, multiple head layouts, partial/full RoPE, independent shuffled/negative slots, untouched cache regions, non-contiguous strides, empty inputs, graph replay after positions/slots changes, and dynamic cache capacity. Runtime JIT reuse does not imply that ACLGraph buckets or captured scalar arguments update automatically.


- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ced6857afa0ea7b2e3f0846a62e1394e90f15607
